title: Model Coinbase collateral as nested assets, liabilities, customer collateral and pledged encumbrances
decisions: Represent the USD1.2995B balance-sheet crypto-assets-held-as-collateral as a total; its USD301.943M recognized derivatives component is nested and must not be added again.
Store recognized lending collateral as USD1.009297B, split into USD997.557M crypto and USD11.740M fiat/payment stablecoins.
Store USD3.284562B customer collateral not recognized as a separate off-balance-sheet category.
Store USD434.163M company-owned assets pledged against short-term borrowings as an encumbrance view; do not add it to recognized collateral without identifying overlap.
Store USD389.657M crypto assets borrowed and USD1.976137B loan receivables as separate measures, not collateral received.
Store the USD1.311240B obligation-to-return-collateral liability separately from collateral assets.
Do not infer XRP exposure from 'other crypto assets'; asset-specific XRP amount remains unknown.
rationale: The SEC filing contains overlapping accounting presentations and separate asset, liability, customer-collateral and company-pledge views. A naive sum would double-count the derivatives component or mix collateral received with collateral pledged. XRP-specific exposure is undisclosed.
limitations: Coinbase's institutional financing and derivatives collateral activity is substantial, but the filing does not establish XRP-specific collateral use.
The earlier USD1.2995B value was correct as the balance-sheet crypto-collateral total; this addendum clarifies that the USD301.943M derivatives amount is nested within it.
The USD434.163M short-term borrowing pledge is a separate encumbrance view, not a new pool to add to the balance-sheet total.
next_action: Seek asset-level collateral disclosure or permitted public regulatory detail; until then keep Coinbase collateral as aggregate institutional context only.
